findings: [P2] operations.py:reset, supervise — Reset races with the supervisor’s ledger read/modify/write. If reset writes a new generation after supervise reads the old ledger, supervise can overwrite that reset with the old generation and blocked budget. The explicit reset is then lost, leaving the service blocked. Serialize ledger updates with a separate lock and re-read the generation inside that lock; test reset racing with start admission and exhaustion.

[P2] backup.py:create, restore — Legacy catalogs are preserved, but their recorded Git commits are not included in the bundle’s required commit set. create collects commit IDs only from Recorder runs, and restore relocates every legacy worktree to the restored primary repository without ensuring its recorded commit exists there. A catalog referencing a detached commit in an allowed worktree can therefore produce a verified backup with missing historical source evidence. Include and validate catalog commit/base_commit objects, or reject unsupported catalogs before publishing the backup.
requirements_checked: Backup/restore confinement, indexed artifact completeness, historical source preservation, and restored execution settings
Primary embedded Beads namespace enforcement and ancestor fallback rejection
Three-start supervisor budget, durable blocking, explicit reset, and no automatic AI job replay
Maintenance SH/EX fencing and old GUI protocol rejection
Staging commit bytes, review and requirement bindings, artifact acknowledgement, and separate owner confirmation
Health probe scope, fixed CI entrypoint, and disabled PCC
